items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: Then this fellow Malone that I told you that started me off on saxophone, the first one that taught me how to spell

ctx.x: And then we -- you know, we started buying records, all of us, maybe I'd buy this one and the other one buy another record. Then, you know, we started like that. Then this fellow Malone that I told you that started me off on saxophone, the first one that taught me how to spell, I'd say, you know, "Spell it," but I couldn't read fast. My cousin trumpet player could. But the fellow Malone, we couldn't keep him. He'd been on the circuses and carnivals and everytime, anytime a carnival came to town, he'd be playing…

But he started me -- like he started me off in playing one of these parties that I told you that Miss Frost arranged for us, you know, the lady that was affiliated with the colleges, a saxophone player -- they had like four theaters that had live music with like six or seven-piece bands in them, in the white theaters and I used to go in the back of the alley and listen to him because he had a beautiful tone on alto. His name was Frank O'Bannon. We -- it was segregated. I couldn't pay to go in, you know, we…
